name: What hidden problems usually show up after demolition?

mainEntity.name: What surprises are most common once demolition starts on an older Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: What surprises are most common once demolition starts on an older Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden problems are one of the biggest risks in a gut renovation. Once walls, floors, and ceilings are opened, contractors often find damage that was impossible to see during the initial walkthrough. Common examples include old wiring that cannot support modern loads, corroded or undersized plumbing, termite damage, dry rot, slab cracks, water leaks, mold, or framing that no longer meets current standards. In some Los Angeles homes, previous owners may have made unpermitted changes that must be corrected before moving forward. These discoveries can increase cost and extend the timeline, so a contingency reserve is essential. Homeowners should ask the contractor how change orders are handled, what evidence is needed before approving extra work, and whether the design team can quickly revise plans if conditions change. The best way to reduce surprises is a thorough preconstruction inspection and careful documentation before demolition starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common hidden issues include outdated wiring, old plumbing, termite damage, dry rot, water intrusion, improper framing, slab problems, and unpermitted changes from previous owners.
